unit: nominal US dollars of assessed value (Wisconsin assesses at market value; the city revalues on its own cycle, so some year-on-year jumps are revaluations, not market moves)
holders: Exemption codes grouped by holder: city, housing-authority (HACM), redevelopment (RACM), city-tax-deed (foreclosed by the city), schools (MPS), county, state, federal, religious, education, hospital, nonprofit, rail-utility, streets, unresolved.

quality.units_1977_1980: Class-1 NUMUNITS runs ~25% above adjacent years (230k vs ~180k); cause unknown. Units series is flagged, not corrected.
quality.units_2019_2021: Non-residential classes (2, 4, 9) carry hotel rooms / beds as units (class 4 jumps 2k -> 64k). Headline housing units use classes 1/5/7 only.
quality.exempt_value_pre_1984: Exempt parcels carry no exempt value before 1984. Public holdings are counted by parcel and lot area only.
quality.exempt_value_2022: The published 2022 file has exempt value for only a fraction of exempt parcels ($0.7B vs ~$5B either side). Not imputed.
quality.convey_date_2009_on: CONVEY_DATE is partly destroyed ("00:00.0", an Excel time-format export artefact) from ~2009, and absent from 2022. Sales counts are reliable only where fill is reported high.
quality.exempt_codes_2004: 2004 uses an exemption numbering seen in no other year. Holders are assigned per parcel where 2003 and 2005 agree; ~225 parcels stay unresolved, and 2004 has no Housing Authority parcels at all (they carry no code that year). Treat 2004 holder counts as approximate.
quality.exempt_lot_area: Lot area on exempt parcels is blank before 1977 and from 2020, and corrupt for some parcels from 2022. Holder acreage is published only for years flagged fields.exemptLotAreaUsable.
quality.units_1975_1976: Residential-class units read 160k (1975) and 223k (1976), against ~235-245k from 1982 on. The early unit fields are incomplete; do not read a housing boom into 1975-1980.
quality.geography: MPROP is the City of Milwaukee only. QCEW and BEA tables are Milwaukee County, which also includes the inner suburbs (~40% of county population).
